This is deliberate: the Data TA’s index-time routing, Filters nullQueue, _time drop, and splunk_solution / cloud_provider stamping all key on sourcetype = sap_logserv_logs (props.conf stanzas match on sourcetype, not index), so it must never vary.

    The index, by contrast, may be changed safely — parsing is unaffected (events are routed, filtered, and stamped identically no matter which index they land in). You may point it at a custom index (for example a per-customer index such as sap_logserv_logs_con01). The only follow-up is dashboard visibility: the dashboards and rollups search through the sap_logserv_idx_macro macro (default index="sap_logserv_logs"), so override that macro in the App’s local/macros.conf to match your index, or the dashboards won’t find the data.

    cloud_provider attribution¶

    The input stamps every event it emits with the indexed field cloud_provider=azure (the add-on’s default/inputs.conf sets _meta = cloud_provider::azure for every input of this kind), so search-time queries and the Multi-Cloud Overview dashboard can distinguish Azure-sourced from AWS-sourced data.

    When you ingest from AWS as well as Azure

    The Data TA’s Configuration → Cloud Provider dropdown stamps cloud_provider TA-wide at index time. If it is set to aws on a forwarder that also runs this Azure input, that index-time stamp co-fires with the input’s per-event _meta=azure, leaving cloud_provider multivalued (azure + aws) on the Azure events. For correct per-channel attribution on a mixed forwarder, set the Cloud Provider dropdown to “Not set” and add _meta = cloud_provider::aws to the Splunk_TA_aws SQS-S3 input — then each input self-attributes. This applies even when AWS and Azure run on separate forwarders: a Deployment Server pushes the dropdown’s value to every forwarder in the SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders server class. Leave the dropdown at Not set on forwarders that run this add-on: its input already stamps cloud_provider, and the dropdown would add the value a second time. A forwarder can run the AWS and Azure add-ons together; see Capacity Planning and First Start → More Than One Cloud for when to separate them. See Choose Cloud Attribution.

    Multiple landscapes / fleets¶

    • Multiple Azure landscapes on one HF: create one input instance per landscape (different account_name / queue_name), using the Inputs table’s Clone action. The per-instance credential is keyed by the input name; re-enter the SAS on each (clone never carries secrets).
    • A fleet of heavy forwarders: install the add-on on each HF that may run an input (still never through the DS). Create the input for a given queue on one HF. Add it on more HFs only for throughput or to catch up a backlog, accepting at-least-once delivery (see the note below); to fail over, enable the standby HF’s input after you disable the first one. For zero-touch fleets, config management can drop the add-on into etc/apps/ and seed the SAS via the REST call above (it encrypts under each HF’s own splunk.secret). Do not add the add-on to the Deployment Server’s deployment-apps/.

    Scaling one queue by cloning — supported (like the AWS add-on), but at-least-once

    Separate input instances are normally for different queues (different queue_name). You can also point several identical inputs at the same queue to raise throughput — this is the same competing-consumer pattern Splunk’s AWS add-on uses to scale its SQS-Based S3 input: the queue’s visibility lease hands each message to one consumer at a time, so N inputs fetch and ingest N batches of blobs in parallel (across one HF, since the input is not single-instance, or across several HFs). Understand the trade-off first:

    • A single input is effectively duplicate-free across the queue’s redelivery window — its per-input dedup checkpoint (<input_name>.dedup.json; entries are retained for about 7 days, up to 50,000 blobs) skips an already-ingested blob if a message reappears.
    • Cloned same-queue inputs don’t share that checkpoint, so they fall back to at-least-once (the same guarantee as the AWS SQS-S3 input). If a message is not deleted within its visibility_timeout (default 300 s), the message reappears and another input re-ingests it → duplicate events. The lease starts when a batch of up to batch_size messages is dequeued, and each message is deleted after its own blobs are done, so what must fit is the time from dequeue to delete for the last message of a batch. The guard is identical to the AWS pattern: set visibility_timeout comfortably above that time. (dequeue_count is the queue’s server-side, shared counter, so the poison_threshold decision stays coordinated across the clones — but unlike SQS, Azure Storage Queue has no native dead-letter/redrive, so poison handling is the TA’s client-side poison_threshold + optional dead_letter_queue.)

    For typical LogServ volumes a single input already keeps up (it drains up to max_blobs_per_fire blobs per firing). Prefer raising batch_size / max_blobs_per_fire or lowering interval on one input before cloning; clone same-queue inputs only when one input genuinely can’t keep up, and raise visibility_timeout when you do.

    Reliability behavior¶

    • At-least-once + dedup. A queue message carrying LogServ blobs is deleted only after those blobs ingest successfully (poison messages and irrelevant / unparseable notifications are removed without ingest — see below); each blob is deduplicated by url|etag in a checkpoint sidecar, so a redelivered message re-ingests nothing.
    • Transient failures leave the message. A 5xx / network error on a blob fetch leaves the message on the queue (it redelivers after the visibility timeout); already-ingested blobs in that message are no-ops on retry.
    • Blob-read denied (401/403) leaves the message and logs loudly — this is the queue-only-SAS signal (get a blob-readable credential from SAP, the message reprocesses).
    • Poison messages (redelivered more than poison_threshold times) are moved to dead_letter_queue if configured, else dropped, so one permanently-bad blob can’t loop forever.

    Historical backfill¶

    Queue-driven ingest is forward-only by nature — Event Grid fires only on new BlobCreated events, so once SAP’s subscription is live the input ingests everything written from that point on (plus the notifications still in the queue when you create the input), but does not replay blobs that already existed. This solution has no historical load for Azure; to load older blobs, agree a method with your Splunk team.

    The add-on reads only the blobs that queue messages name and never lists the container. A day whose notifications were purged, or expired before the input read them, stays in SAP’s storage, but nothing in Splunk for SAP LogServ will load it. If you will need such days, agree with your Splunk team how to load them before you ask SAP to purge anything (see First Start: The Queue Backlog).

    When filtering is on, the Data TA’s Days in the Past filter applies to everything the input reads, the queue backlog included: events older than its cutoff are dropped before indexing.

    Rotate credentials¶

    The SAS stops working at its expiry time, the se= value in the SAS string. From then on every queue read fails with HTTP 403 (queue read failed (... 403 ...); aborting firing in the input log), and the input ingests nothing. The notifications wait in the queue only as long as their time-to-live allows (7 days by default); days whose notifications expire before you replace the SAS cannot be loaded later (see Historical backfill).

    To replace the SAS:

    1. Ask your SAP support contact for the new SAS before the current one expires. Check its scope and expiry as in What the SAP-provided SAS must cover.
    2. On the instance that runs the input, open Apps → Splunk TA for SAP LogServ on Azure → Inputs and choose Edit on the input. The SAS token field shows ******.
    3. Replace ****** with the new SAS and click Update. Saving needs a role that holds admin_all_objects. (If you leave ****** in the field, the stored SAS is kept.)
    4. The input reads the SAS at every firing, so the next firing uses the new one. Check the input log for a done: line and no queue read failed (see Validation).
    5. Repeat on every other instance that has an input using this SAS, such as a standby heavy forwarder. Each instance keeps its own encrypted copy in the add-on’s local/passwords.conf; the Deployment Server does not carry it.

    Then put the new se= date in your calendar.

    Validation¶

    Confirm the input is registered and firing (run on the heavy forwarder):

    curl -sk -u admin:<pwd> \
  "https://localhost:8089/servicesNS/nobody/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure_sap_logserv_azure_queue?output_mode=json"

    Watch the input log on the HF:

    sudo tail -f /opt/splunk/var/log/splunk/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure_queue.log
# look for:  Input 'logserv_azure' done: messages=N blobs=N events=N dups=N deleted=N ...

    Search the indexer (events route to per-source sourcetypes just like AWS):

    index=sap_logserv_logs cloud_provider=azure _index_earliest=-1h | stats count by sourcetype

    For the full set of checks (sourcetypes, one cloud_provider value per event, routing), see Verify Your Data.

    Troubleshooting¶

    Symptom (in the input log unless noted) Cause Fix
    Splunk Web shows “This operation is forbidden” (HTTP 403) when you save, edit or delete an input The signed-in role lacks the admin_all_objects capability Use a role that holds admin_all_objects on this instance (see Configure the input).
    SAS token not found in passwords.conf; skipping No credential for this input name on this host Re-enter the SAS on this HF (Inputs tab → Edit, or the REST call above). The SAS lives in the add-on’s own local/passwords.conf; it is not affected by Deployment-Server pushes.
    queue read failed (... 403 ...) The SAS has expired (se= has passed), or it lacks queue process (p), or ss lacks q, or srt lacks o Decode the SAS (see What the SAP-provided SAS must cover). If it has expired, get a new one from SAP and replace it. Otherwise ask SAP for a SAS with ss ⊇ q, srt ⊇ o, sp ⊇ p and a future se=. d is not needed: Delete does not apply to queue messages in an account SAS, and p already covers Delete Message.
    blob read forbidden (HTTP 401/403) SAS is queue-only (no blob read) or expired Ask SAP for a blob-readable SAS (ss ⊇ b, sp ⊇ r); the message is left for retry.
    done: messages=0 every firing, but blobs exist The Event Grid subscription (SAP-managed) isn’t enqueuing, or the queue name is wrong Confirm with your SAP support contact that the Event Grid subscription is active and the queue name is correct; verify network egress to <account>.queue.core.windows.net.
    Input kind sap_logserv_azure_queue not listed / Inputs page missing The Azure add-on isn’t installed (or Splunkd wasn’t restarted) on this HF Install splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure on the HF and restart (see Install the Azure add-on).

    For problems that are not specific to the Azure input, see Troubleshooting.

    Next steps¶

    • Verify Your Data: check that events arrive with the expected sourcetypes and one cloud_provider value
    • Check the LogServ App prerequisites, then install the LogServ App on your Search Head
    • Review the supported log types reference
    • For Splunk Cloud considerations, see Splunk Cloud Considerations

    SAP LogServ on GCP — Setup Guide¶

    This page covers ingesting LogServ data from Google Cloud Storage (GCS) using the standalone LogServ GCP add-on (splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp, shown in Splunk Web as Splunk TA for SAP LogServ on GCP) and its sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub modular input — the GCP twin of Splunk_TA_aws’s SQS-Based S3 input and of the LogServ Azure add-on’s Storage-Queue input. A GCS bucket notification publishes an OBJECT_FINALIZE message to a Pub/Sub topic; this input pulls a Pub/Sub subscription on that topic, fetches each named object with a Google service-account key, gunzips it, and emits its NDJSON. This is the model SAP’s own LogServ-on-GCP collector uses (Pub/Sub object-creation notifications). You install this small, first-party add-on on the heavy forwarder that runs the input — the same deployment model as the Splunk Add-on for AWS and the LogServ Azure add-on — and the LogServ Data TA on the same instance provides the downstream sourcetype routing, filtering, and stamping. The downstream pipeline (sourcetype routing, filtering, dashboards, ES integration) is identical to the AWS S3 and Azure Blob paths.

    SAP provides the GCP infrastructure — you provide the service account that reads it

    In a RISE / SAP ECS deployment the GCS bucket, bucket notification, Pub/Sub topic, and Pub/Sub subscription are all provisioned and managed by SAP in the SAP-managed GCP project. You do not build any of that. What you do provide is the identity the Splunk input runs as: a service account you create in a GCP project of your own (any project your organization controls, separate from the SAP-managed RISE project). You hand the service account’s email address to your SAP support contact, SAP grants it read access to the LogServ bucket + Pub/Sub subscription, and you mint its JSON key for the Splunk input — see The onboarding sequence. On the Splunk side your tasks are to install the splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp add-on on the heavy forwarder that will run the input and create one Splunk input per Pub/Sub subscription on it — one per GCP landscape (most deployments have a single landscape, hence one input; you can define several on the same HF if you ingest from more than one — see Multiple landscapes / fleets), using the values from Parameters for the input.

    High Level Steps¶

    Follow these steps in order. Each step links to its section below.

    1. Create the service account and get SAP’s grants: create it in your own GCP project, give its email to SAP, and get back the project ID and subscription name. Enable the two Google APIs and mint the JSON key (check your organization’s key policy first). See The onboarding sequence.
    2. Decide about the subscription backlog with SAP before the input exists. A purged day cannot be loaded later. See First Start: The Queue Backlog and Historical backfill.
    3. Check the Data TA and the indexes. The Data TA must be on the instance that will run the input, and the indexes must exist, before the input reads anything: events indexed without the Data TA keep the base sourcetype for good. See Prerequisites.
    4. Download and install the add-on on that instance, directly (never through the Deployment Server). See Install the GCP add-on.
    5. Before the input starts, check the Data TA’s two index-time settings. Leave Cloud Provider at Not set: the input stamps cloud_provider=gcp itself (see cloud_provider attribution and Choose Cloud Attribution). Decide filtering (see Decide Filtering). Whatever the subscription holds when the input starts is indexed with the settings in place at that moment.
    6. Create one input for the subscription, with a role that holds admin_all_objects. See Configure the input.
    7. Check that data arrives. See Validation.
    8. Plan the key rotation your security policy requires. See Rotate credentials.

    Architecture overview¶

    SAP LogServ RISE-ECS  (SAP-managed GCP project)
  |
  +-> writes NDJSON.gz objects to Google Cloud Storage under the logserv/ prefix
        |
        +-> GCS bucket notification (OBJECT_FINALIZE)
              |
              +-> Pub/Sub topic --> Pub/Sub PULL subscription (one message per new object)
                    |
                    |    [Customer GCP account]  service account created by YOU;
                    |    SAP grants it read access to the LogServ bucket + subscription;
                    |    its JSON key authenticates the Splunk input below
                    |
                    +-> [GCP add-on: sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub]  (runs on the Heavy Forwarder)
                          |   pulls the subscription, fetches each object with the
                          |   service-account credential, gunzips, splits NDJSON
                          |
                          +-> emits via EventWriter, sourcetype=sap_logserv_logs, cloud_provider=gcp
                                |
                                +-> [LogServ Data TA pipeline]  (same Heavy Forwarder):
                                      sourcetype routing by clz_dir/clz_subdir or source path,
                                      Configuration -> Filters nullQueue, _time drop,
                                      splunk_solution stamping
                                      |
                                      +-> forwarded to the Indexer
                                            |
                                            +-> dashboards + ES integration

    Everything from the LogServ object writer down through the Pub/Sub subscription lives in the SAP-managed GCP project and is managed by SAP. The one piece homed on your side of GCP is the service account: it lives in a GCP project you manage (the Customer GCP account box in the diagram), SAP grants it cross-project read access to the LogServ subscription + bucket, and its JSON key is what the Splunk input authenticates with — the GCP analogue of the AWS path’s customer-account cross-account IAM role. The GCP add-on’s sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub input runs on your heavy forwarder, pulls the subscription SAP exposes to you, and hands its events to the LogServ Data TA (also on that HF) for routing/filtering/stamping. This is exactly how Splunk_TA_aws and the LogServ Azure add-on cooperate with the Data TA on their respective paths.

    Why EventWriter, not HEC: the input runs on the heavy forwarder and emits through the HF’s native index-time pipeline, so every existing LogServ Data TA feature — sourcetype routing (by the clz_dir / clz_subdir folder fields or by the source path, depending on the log type; see Supported Log Types), the Configuration → Filters nullQueue filtering, the days_in_past / _time drop, and the splunk_solution stamping — applies to GCP events unchanged, exactly as it does to AWS S3 and Azure Blob events. The cloud_provider value comes from the add-on itself (see cloud_provider attribution). The input is stdlib-only (Pub/Sub + GCS REST over urllib, with a pure-Python OAuth2 service-account token exchange — no Google SDK), so it adds no AArch64 / native-binary burden and is Splunk Cloud-clean.

    Prerequisites¶

    Provided by SAP (in the SAP-managed GCP project — you obtain the values, you do not build the resources):

    • A GCS bucket holding the LogServ objects (under the logserv/ prefix — same path convention as AWS S3 and Azure Blob: <bucket>/logserv/<clz_dir>/<clz_subdir>/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<file>.json.gz).
    • A bucket notification publishing OBJECT_FINALIZE events to a Pub/Sub topic, and a PULL subscription on that topic dedicated to your Splunk consumer (recommended: ack deadline 300 s+ and a dead-letter policy).
    • The cross-project IAM grants on those resources for the service account you provide (see below).

    Obtain the GCP project ID and the subscription name from your SAP support contact — see Parameters for the input.

    Provided by you in GCP (the service account — see The onboarding sequence):

    • A GCP project of your own: any project your organization controls, separate from the SAP-managed RISE project (the Customer GCP account in the diagram, and the GCP counterpart of the Secondary account in the AWS guides). No infrastructure is deployed in it — it is only the administrative home of the identity.
    • A service account created in that project. You hand its email address to your SAP support contact, and SAP grants it roles/pubsub.subscriber on the LogServ subscription and roles/storage.objectViewer on the LogServ bucket (see What SAP must grant your service account).
    • A JSON key for that service account, minted by your GCP admin (check the org-policy warning in The onboarding sequence before install day).
    • The Cloud Pub/Sub API and Cloud Storage API enabled in the service account’s home project (Google attributes API quota to the credential’s home project, not to the project holding the resources).

    On your Splunk side (the instance that runs the input — a heavy forwarder is strongly recommended):

    • LogServ Data TA 0.1.1+ installed on that instance (it provides the index-time routing/filtering/stamping; see Installing the Data TA). On heavy forwarders the Data TA is normally distributed by the Deployment Server (see Distribute the Data TA to Heavy Forwarders). Its build decides the parsing cost on the forwarder: use build 1792189743 or later, and see Version Check to read the build on a forwarder.
    • The indexes (sap_logserv_logs, and the AI Assistant audit index) on your indexer tier, before any data arrives. See Create the indexes.
    • LogServ GCP add-on (splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp) 0.1.1+ installed on the same instance (see Install the GCP add-on). It registers the sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub input kind. The input is inert until you create an input instance.
    • A Splunk role that holds the admin_all_objects capability on that instance, to create, edit or delete the input (see Configure the input).
    • Network egress from that instance to oauth2.googleapis.com, pubsub.googleapis.com, and storage.googleapis.com (port 443 / HTTPS). The add-on has no proxy setting of its own; if the instance reaches the internet through a proxy, see Outbound proxy under Heavy Forwarders.

    Compact JSON format required

    Each object is gzipped NDJSON (one event per line). The index-time routing transforms assume compact JSON (no whitespace after :). The SAP LogServ collector emits compact JSON natively, so no action is required on your side. (For reference: pretty-printed JSON would bypass the transforms and land as sourcetype=sap_logserv_logs, breaking dashboards.)

    Parameters for the input¶

    SAP has already provisioned the bucket, notification, topic, and subscription in the SAP-managed GCP project — the only GCP resource you create is the service account (The onboarding sequence). Contact your SAP support contact to obtain the two SAP-side values, then plug them — plus your own service-account key — into the Splunk input (Configure the input):

    Parameter Input field Provided by Description
    GCP project ID project_id SAP The GCP project that hosts the LogServ Pub/Sub subscription (SAP’s LogServ project — e.g. the LOGSERV_PROJECT_ID value SAP’s own forwarder documentation references). 6–30 chars: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; starts with a letter, ends with a letter or digit.
    Subscription name subscription_name SAP The Pub/Sub PULL subscription receiving the bucket’s OBJECT_FINALIZE notifications. Must be dedicated to your Splunk consumer (competing consumers split messages).
    Service-account key service_account_key You The full Google service-account JSON key file contents, minted from the service account you created in your own GCP project (after SAP confirms the grants). Treat it as a secret.

    The bucket name and logserv/ prefix are carried inside each notification message — they are not separate input fields. The three Google endpoints your heavy forwarder must reach are fixed (oauth2.googleapis.com, pubsub.googleapis.com, storage.googleapis.com).

    Ask SAP also for the subscription’s ack deadline (300 s or more is recommended); the input’s batch_size must fit inside it (see Scaling one subscription across inputs below).

    The onboarding sequence¶

    The service account is customer-homed: it lives in a GCP project you control (the Customer GCP account in the architecture diagram), and SAP binds cross-project grants on the SAP-managed LogServ resources to it. Nothing is deployed in your project — it is only the administrative home of the identity. The sequence:

    1. Create the service account in a GCP project your organization controls: IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Create service account. A descriptive name such as splunk-logserv-ingest helps everyone’s audit trail. The account needs no roles in your own project.
    2. Hand the service account’s email address (<name>@<your-project-id>.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to your SAP support contact and request LogServ consumer access for it.
    3. SAP grants the account roles/pubsub.subscriber on the LogServ subscription and roles/storage.objectViewer on the LogServ bucket (cross-project IAM bindings on the SAP-managed resources — see What SAP must grant your service account), and returns the project ID and subscription name values for the input.
    4. Enable the Cloud Pub/Sub API and the Cloud Storage API in the service account’s home project (APIs & Services → Enable APIs and services). Google attributes API quota to the credential’s home project, so a missing enablement fails the first connection with 403 SERVICE_DISABLED naming your project (see Troubleshooting).
    5. Mint the JSON key: IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → (the account) → Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON, and stage the downloaded file for the input configuration. (Read the org-policy warning below first.)
    6. Configure the input on the heavy forwarder that will run it (Configure the input) once SAP confirms the grants are in place.

    Organization policy can block key creation entirely

    Many enterprises enforce the iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation organization policy as a security guardrail. If it applies to the service account’s home project, minting a JSON key fails regardless of IAM roles — your admin needs roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin on the account and a policy exemption for it. Check this before install day; it is the most common last-minute blocker.

    What SAP must grant your service account¶

    The input pulls/acks subscription messages and fetches objects with the single service account you provide, so SAP must bind both grants to its email. Confirm with your SAP support contact that your account holds:

    IAM role Scope For
    roles/pubsub.subscriber the LogServ subscription pull + acknowledge notification messages
    roles/storage.objectViewer the LogServ bucket fetch the referenced objects

    These two roles are the complete runtime set — the input makes exactly four Google API calls (OAuth token mint, subscriptions:pull, subscriptions:acknowledge, and the object download), all covered by the grants above. They are the same two roles SAP documents for its own sap-ecs-gcp-log-forwarder consumer. Unlike the general-purpose Splunk Add-on for GCP, this input needs no extra roles/pubsub.viewer grant (that add-on calls GetSubscription; this input never does) — don’t ask SAP to over-grant.

    If the grant is subscription-only

    If your service account lacks roles/storage.objectViewer on the bucket, object fetches fail with HTTP 403 and the input logs it explicitly: “object read forbidden … the service account likely lacks storage.objectViewer on the bucket; leaving message for retry.” The decisive question for your SAP support contact is “has my service account been granted read on the bucket’s objects, or only the subscription?” If it is subscription-only, ask SAP to add the bucket-read grant (a second credential is not supported — the input uses one account for both).

    Install the GCP add-on¶

    Download splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp-0.1.2.tar.gz from the release_binaries folder of the Splunk for SAP LogServ GitHub repository. Its AppInspect report sits beside it, and the folder’s README.md lists each tarball’s md5. The build and md5 of each package are also listed under Download the Packages.

    Install it directly on the instance that runs the input. A heavy forwarder is strongly recommended — it is the tier where Splunk_TA_aws (AWS) and the LogServ Azure add-on (Azure) run for their paths. A search head is not blocked (see Running the TAs on a search head). You can install the add-on on every heavy forwarder that may run an input, for example to keep a standby ready; the input for a given subscription still runs on one of them (see Configure the input).

    • Splunk Web → Manage Apps → Install app from file → upload the tarball, or
    • /opt/splunk/bin/splunk install app /path/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp-0.1.2.tar.gz, or
    • configuration management (Ansible / Puppet / Chef) drops the app into etc/apps/, then chown -R splunk:splunk and restart.

    Do NOT distribute the GCP add-on via the Deployment Server

    Install it directly on each instance that runs an input — never as a deployment-app. The input’s service-account key is stored, encrypted, in the add-on’s own local/passwords.conf; a Deployment Server push replaces the app’s local/ directory, which would wipe the per-HF credential. (This is the same reason Splunk_TA_aws and the LogServ Azure add-on are configured per-HF rather than DS-distributed.) The Data TA stays DS-managed as before — only the cloud-ingest add-ons are per-HF.

    After installing + restarting, the sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub input kind is registered and the add-on’s Inputs page is available under Apps → Splunk TA for SAP LogServ on GCP.

    Upgrading from an earlier build? See Upgrading to This Release.

    Single instance¶

    On a single Splunk Enterprise instance (no separate forwarder or indexer), install the Data TA and the GCP add-on on that instance and create the input there, as described below. The Data TA’s bundled indexes.conf creates both indexes on that instance; set the retention of sap_logserv_logs if you want one other than the default (see Create the indexes). There is no Deployment Server step: the Data TA’s settings are saved on the instance itself. The LogServ App goes on the same instance.

    Splunk Cloud¶

    With Splunk Cloud, run the input on a heavy forwarder you manage:

    1. Create both indexes in your Splunk Cloud stack first (Settings → Indexes, or the Admin Config Service), with the retention you want, before any data arrives. See Create the indexes.
    2. Set the heavy forwarder up to forward to your stack, with your stack’s universal forwarder credentials app installed on it.
    3. Put the Data TA on the heavy forwarder (through your Deployment Server, or directly if you have none), and install the GCP add-on on it directly, as above.
    4. Create the input on the heavy forwarder (Configure the input).

    The LogServ App goes on the Splunk Cloud search head. The Data TA is not needed on the Cloud stack in this layout.

    Without a heavy forwarder. The add-on’s app.manifest declares the search-head workload, so a search head is an allowed target for it; installing it on a Splunk Cloud search head has not been tested. In this layout, install the Data TA and the GCP add-on on the search head as private apps, and create the input there. The Data TA must sit beside the add-on, because it parses the events where the input runs. We strongly recommend against this layout, because the input puts ingest load on the tier your users search on. Creating the input needs a role that holds admin_all_objects there too. See Running the TAs on a search head and Splunk Cloud Considerations.

    Configure the input¶

    Create one input for each Pub/Sub subscription, on one instance (normally one heavy forwarder). You can install the add-on on every HF, for example to keep a standby ready, but run the input for a given subscription on one HF only. Every other input on the same subscription, on the same HF or another one, keeps its own dedup record, so a redelivered message can be indexed twice (see Scaling one subscription across inputs below). The service-account key is encrypted into the add-on’s own local/passwords.conf and is not Deployment-Server-managed — it survives restarts and Data-TA pushes.

    Creating or editing an input needs admin_all_objects

    On Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud alike, creating, editing (including replacing the service-account key) and deleting an input runs as the signed-in user and needs a role that holds the admin_all_objects capability. Without it, Save fails with HTTP 403, “This operation is forbidden”. The REST call below has the same requirement.

    A new input starts with what is already in the subscription

    The subscription may already hold notifications from before your input exists: up to 7 days of them by default, and up to 31 days if SAP keeps messages longer. A new input works through all of them on top of the live feed. Before you create it, see First Start: The Queue Backlog, which includes asking SAP to purge the older messages. The add-on cannot load purged days later (see Historical backfill).

    Via Splunk Web (per Heavy Forwarder)¶

    Splunk Web → Apps → Splunk TA for SAP LogServ on GCP → Inputs → Create New Input, and fill in the fields below with the project ID + subscription name from SAP — and paste the entire JSON key file of your own service account into the key field. (For a second landscape on the same HF, use the Inputs table’s Clone action and give it a new name — the key is not carried on clone, so re-paste it. On Edit, the key field shows ******; saving without changing it preserves the existing key.)

    Paste the whole file — not just the private key

    The key field takes the complete downloaded .json file, verbatim — everything from the opening { to the closing } ("type": "service_account", "project_id", "private_key", "client_email", and the rest). Open the file in a text editor, Select All, copy, paste.

    • Keep the -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- and -----END PRIVATE KEY----- lines. They are part of the private_key value inside the JSON — do not remove them, and do not un-escape the \n sequences around them.
    • Do not extract the private key out of the JSON. The add-on parses the pasted text as JSON (it reads client_email, private_key, and token_uri from it); a bare key — with or without the BEGIN/END lines — is not valid JSON and is rejected at the first poll with service-account key unusable.

    Via REST (scriptable, per Heavy Forwarder)¶

    # Stage the service-account JSON key file, then create the input:
curl -sk -u admin:<pwd> -X POST \
  https://localhost:8089/servicesNS/nobody/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp_sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub \
  --data-urlencode name=logserv_gcp \
  --data-urlencode project_id=<sap-logserv-project-id> \
  --data-urlencode subscription_name=<subscription-name> \
  --data-urlencode index=sap_logserv_logs \
  --data-urlencode event_sourcetype=sap_logserv_logs \
  --data-urlencode interval=60 \
  --data-urlencode service_account_key@/tmp/logserv-sa-key.json
rm -f /tmp/logserv-sa-key.json

    The resulting stanza in the add-on’s local/inputs.conf looks like:

    [sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub://logserv_gcp]
project_id = <sap-logserv-project-id>
subscription_name = <subscription-name>
service_account_key = ******
index = sap_logserv_logs
event_sourcetype = sap_logserv_logs
interval = 60
disabled = 0

    (Only the masked placeholder service_account_key = ****** is written to inputs.conf — the real key is stored encrypted in the add-on’s own local/passwords.conf.)

    Field Default Notes
    project_id — The SAP LogServ GCP project ID from SAP (6–30 chars: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; must start with a letter and end with a letter or digit).
    subscription_name — The Pub/Sub PULL subscription name from SAP (receives the OBJECT_FINALIZE notifications).
    service_account_key — The complete JSON key file of the service account you created in your own GCP project (The onboarding sequence), pasted verbatim — including the -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- / -----END PRIVATE KEY----- lines inside the private_key value. Encrypted credential: the value lives in the add-on’s local/passwords.conf; inputs.conf carries only the masked ****** placeholder.
    index sap_logserv_logs Target index. Does not affect parsing — the Data TA’s index-time pipeline keys on the sourcetype, not the index. You may point it at a custom index, but the dashboards query through the sap_logserv_idx_macro macro, so update that macro to match (see caveat below).
    event_sourcetype (UI label Sourcetype) sap_logserv_logs Fixed at sap_logserv_logs. The add-on hard-codes this sourcetype (it is not read from the stanza), and the field is shown read-only when editing the input. Leave it at the default.
    interval 60 Seconds between firings (10–3600). Each firing drains the subscription within a per-firing time budget (currently 90% of interval, capped at 240 s) and the max_objects_per_fire cap.
    batch_size 10 Pub/Sub messages requested per pull call (maxMessages, 1–1000). The input acknowledges a batch only after processing all of it, so a whole batch must finish within the subscription’s ack deadline.
    max_objects_per_fire 500 Cap on objects ingested per firing (backlog safety valve).
    poison_threshold 5 A message redelivered more than this many times (Pub/Sub deliveryAttempt) is acked and dropped. See Reliability behavior.
    include_filters / exclude_filters (empty) Optional comma-separated substrings applied to the GCS object path as a cheap pre-filter (beyond the built-in logserv match). The canonical allow/deny policy lives in the Data TA’s Filters tab.
    verify_ssl 1 TLS verification for the Google API endpoints. Leave enabled for production.

    Sourcetype is fixed; the Index is yours to change

    The Sourcetype is effectively fixed at sap_logserv_logs — the add-on always emits it (the value is hard-coded in the input, not read from the stanza), and the field is shown read-only (disabled) when editing an existing input. When you create an input the field can still be typed into, but whatever you enter is ignored and the add-on still emits sap_logserv_logs. This is deliberate: the Data TA’s index-time routing, Filters nullQueue, _time drop, and splunk_solution / cloud_provider stamping all key on sourcetype = sap_logserv_logs (props.conf stanzas match on sourcetype, not index), so it must never vary.

    The index, by contrast, may be changed safely — parsing is unaffected (events are routed, filtered, and stamped identically no matter which index they land in). You may point it at a custom index (for example a per-customer index such as sap_logserv_logs_con01). The only follow-up is dashboard visibility: the dashboards and rollups search through the sap_logserv_idx_macro macro (default index="sap_logserv_logs"), so override that macro in the App’s local/macros.conf to match your index, or the dashboards won’t find the data.

    cloud_provider attribution¶

    The input stamps every event it emits with the indexed field cloud_provider=gcp (the add-on’s default/inputs.conf sets _meta = cloud_provider::gcp for every input of this kind), so search-time queries and the Multi-Cloud Overview dashboard can distinguish GCP-sourced from AWS- and Azure-sourced data.

    When you ingest from more than one cloud

    The Data TA’s Configuration → Cloud Provider dropdown stamps cloud_provider TA-wide at index time. If it is set to aws (or any provider) on a forwarder that also runs this GCP input, that index-time stamp co-fires with the input’s per-event _meta=gcp, leaving cloud_provider multivalued on the GCP events. For correct per-channel attribution on a mixed forwarder, set the Cloud Provider dropdown to “Not set” and attribute per input: this GCP input and the LogServ Azure add-on’s input already self-attribute via _meta; add _meta = cloud_provider::aws to the Splunk_TA_aws SQS-S3 input. This applies even when each cloud runs on separate forwarders: a Deployment Server pushes the dropdown’s value to every forwarder in the SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders server class. Leave the dropdown at Not set on forwarders that run this add-on: its input already stamps cloud_provider, and the dropdown would add the value a second time. A forwarder can run the GCP add-on beside the AWS or Azure add-on; see Capacity Planning and First Start → More Than One Cloud for when to separate them. See Choose Cloud Attribution.

    Multiple landscapes / fleets¶

    • Multiple GCP landscapes on one HF: create one input instance per landscape (different project_id / subscription_name), using the Inputs table’s Clone action. The per-instance credential is keyed by the input name; re-paste the key on each (clone never carries secrets).
    • A fleet of heavy forwarders: install the add-on on each HF that may run an input (still never through the DS). Create the input for a given subscription on one HF. Add it on more HFs only for throughput or to catch up a backlog, accepting at-least-once delivery (see the note below); to fail over, enable the standby HF’s input after you disable the first one. For zero-touch fleets, config management can drop the add-on into etc/apps/ and seed the key via the REST call above (it encrypts under each HF’s own splunk.secret). Do not add the add-on to the Deployment Server’s deployment-apps/.

    Scaling one subscription across inputs — Pub/Sub is natively competing-consumer

    Separate input instances are normally for different subscriptions. You can also point several identical inputs at the same subscription to raise throughput — competing consumers are Pub/Sub’s native delivery model: N inputs (across one HF or several) pull and ingest N batches of objects in parallel. Pub/Sub tries not to give a message that is still outstanding to another consumer, but it may rarely redeliver any message, even after it was acknowledged, so several consumers can produce occasional duplicates even within the ack deadline (Google’s subscription overview). Understand the trade-off first:

    • A single input is effectively duplicate-free across the subscription’s redelivery window — its per-input dedup checkpoint (keyed bucket/object#generation; entries are retained for about 7 days, up to 50,000 objects) skips an already-ingested object if a message reappears.
    • Same-subscription inputs don’t share that checkpoint, so they fall back to at-least-once (the same guarantee as the AWS SQS-S3 input). If a message is not acknowledged within the subscription’s ack deadline (SAP-managed; 300 s recommended), the message redelivers and another input may re-ingest it → duplicate events. The guard: the input acknowledges once per pull batch, after processing every message in it, so a whole batch (batch_size objects, default 10) must finish within the ack deadline. Ask SAP what the deadline is (Pub/Sub’s default is 10 s), and lower batch_size if it is short. deliveryAttempt is Pub/Sub’s server-side, shared counter, so the poison_threshold decision stays coordinated across the consumers, and a subscription-level dead-letter policy (SAP-managed) handles poison messages natively.

    For typical LogServ volumes a single input already keeps up (it drains up to max_objects_per_fire objects per firing). Prefer raising max_objects_per_fire or lowering interval on one input before adding consumers; raise batch_size only while a whole batch still finishes within the subscription’s ack deadline.

    Reliability behavior¶

    • At-least-once + dedup. A subscription message carrying a LogServ object is acknowledged only after that object ingests successfully (unparseable / non-OBJECT_FINALIZE notifications and paths your filters reject are acknowledged without ingest and counted as noise= in the done log line; poison messages likewise — see below); each object is deduplicated by bucket/object#generation in a checkpoint sidecar, so a redelivered message re-ingests nothing.
    • Transient failures leave the message. A 5xx / network error on an object fetch leaves the message unacknowledged (it redelivers after the ack deadline); already-ingested objects in that message are no-ops on retry.
    • Object-read denied (HTTP 403) leaves the message and logs loudly — this is the missing-storage.objectViewer signal (get the bucket-read grant from SAP; the message reprocesses).
    • Pull denied (HTTP 403) aborts the firing — the service account lacks roles/pubsub.subscriber (or the project/subscription values are wrong); nothing is consumed until the credential is fixed.
    • Deleted objects (HTTP 404) are acked and skipped — an object that vanished between notification and fetch can’t loop.
    • Poison messages (redelivered more than poison_threshold times, per Pub/Sub’s deliveryAttempt counter) are acked and dropped so one permanently-bad object can’t loop forever. deliveryAttempt is populated only when the subscription has a dead-letter policy — with one attached, Pub/Sub also dead-letters natively (the primary mechanism; the TA’s threshold is a local backstop).

    Historical backfill¶

    Notification-driven ingest is forward-only by nature — the bucket notification fires only on new OBJECT_FINALIZE events, so once SAP’s notification is live the input ingests everything written from that point on (plus the messages still in the subscription when you create the input), but does not replay objects that already existed. This solution has no historical load for GCP; to load older objects, agree a method with your Splunk team.

    The add-on reads only the objects that subscription messages name and never lists the bucket. A day whose messages were purged, or expired before the input read them, stays in SAP’s bucket, but nothing in Splunk for SAP LogServ will load it. If you will need such days, agree with your Splunk team how to load them before you ask SAP to purge anything (see First Start: The Queue Backlog). Moving SAP’s subscription forward in time (a seek) acknowledges the older messages; they can be replayed later only if SAP’s subscription keeps acknowledged messages or its topic keeps messages, so ask SAP before a seek.

    When filtering is on, the Data TA’s Days in the Past filter applies to everything the input reads, the subscription backlog included: events older than its cutoff are dropped before indexing.

    Rotate credentials¶

    A service-account key keeps working until it is disabled or deleted in your GCP project, or until it expires if your organization’s policy gives keys an expiry time (the constraints/iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours organization policy; without it, a key never expires). When the key stops working, token minting fails (token minting failed (...); aborting firing in the input log), and the input ingests nothing. The messages wait in the subscription only as long as its message retention allows (7 days by default); days whose messages are removed before you replace the key cannot be loaded later (see Historical backfill). Rotate the key on the schedule your security policy sets.

    To rotate the key:

    1. In your GCP project, add a new JSON key to the service account: IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → (the account) → Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON. A service account can hold up to 10 keys, so the old key keeps working meanwhile. The organization-policy warning applies to new keys too.
    2. On the instance that runs the input, open Apps → Splunk TA for SAP LogServ on GCP → Inputs and choose Edit on the input. The Service-account key (JSON) field shows ******.
    3. Replace ****** with the whole new JSON key file (see Paste the whole file above) and click Update. Saving needs a role that holds admin_all_objects. (If you leave ****** in the field, the stored key is kept.)
    4. The input reads the key at every firing, so the next firing uses the new one. Check the input log for a done: line and no token minting failed (see Validation).
    5. Repeat on every other instance that has an input using this key, such as a standby heavy forwarder. Each instance keeps its own encrypted copy in the add-on’s local/passwords.conf; the Deployment Server does not carry it.
    6. Then disable or delete the old key in your GCP project (Keys tab of the service account).

    SAP’s grants are bound to the service account’s email, not to a key, so a new key needs nothing from SAP.

    Validation¶

    Confirm the input is registered and firing (run on the heavy forwarder):

    curl -sk -u admin:<pwd> \
  "https://localhost:8089/servicesNS/nobody/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp_sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub?output_mode=json"

    Watch the input log on the HF:

    sudo tail -f /opt/splunk/var/log/splunk/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub.log
# look for:  Input 'logserv_gcp' done: messages=N objects=N events=N dups=N acked=N ...

    Search the indexer (events route to per-source sourcetypes just like AWS and Azure):

    index=sap_logserv_logs cloud_provider=gcp _index_earliest=-1h | stats count by sourcetype

    For the full set of checks (sourcetypes, one cloud_provider value per event, routing), see Verify Your Data.

    Troubleshooting¶

    Symptom (in the input log unless noted) Cause Fix
    Splunk Web shows “This operation is forbidden” (HTTP 403) when you save, edit or delete an input The signed-in role lacks the admin_all_objects capability Use a role that holds admin_all_objects on this instance (see Configure the input).
    service-account key not found in passwords.conf; skipping No credential for this input name on this host Re-enter the key on this HF (Inputs tab → Edit, or the REST call above). The key lives in the add-on’s own local/passwords.conf; it is not affected by Deployment-Server pushes.
    service-account key unusable (...) The pasted key is not a valid service-account JSON key (truncated paste, wrong file, or only the bare private key was pasted instead of the whole JSON file) Re-paste the entire JSON key file verbatim — the full {...} document, with the -----BEGIN/END PRIVATE KEY----- lines left intact inside the private_key value.
    token minting failed (...) The key is disabled, deleted or expired, the HF can’t reach oauth2.googleapis.com, or the system clock is skewed (JWTs are time-signed) Verify egress to oauth2.googleapis.com:443 and NTP sync; check in your GCP console whether the key is still active (IAM & Admin → Service Accounts → Keys), and if it is not, mint a new one and replace it.
    subscription pull failed (... 403 ...) SAP’s roles/pubsub.subscriber grant for your service account is missing or not yet applied, or project_id/subscription_name are wrong Confirm the values with your SAP support contact and that the grant for your service account’s email is in place on this subscription (The onboarding sequence).
    subscription pull failed (HTTP 403: … SERVICE_DISABLED …) naming the service account’s home project (“…API has not been used in project…”) The service account is homed in your GCP project, a different project from the LogServ resources, and the Pub/Sub or Cloud Storage API isn’t enabled there (Google attributes API quota to the credential’s home project) Enable the Cloud Pub/Sub API and Cloud Storage API in the account’s home project and retry (step 4 of The onboarding sequence).
    object read forbidden (HTTP 403) The service account lacks roles/storage.objectViewer on the bucket Ask SAP to add the bucket-read grant for your service account’s email; the message is left for retry and reprocesses once fixed.
    done: messages=0 every firing, but objects exist The bucket notification (SAP-managed) isn’t publishing, or the subscription name is wrong Confirm with your SAP support contact that the OBJECT_FINALIZE notification and subscription are active; verify egress to pubsub.googleapis.com.
    Input kind sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub not listed / Inputs page missing The GCP add-on isn’t installed (or Splunkd wasn’t restarted) on this HF Install splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp on the HF and restart (see Install the GCP add-on).

    For problems that are not specific to the GCP input, see Troubleshooting.

    Next steps¶

    • Verify Your Data: check that events arrive with the expected sourcetypes and one cloud_provider value
    • Check the LogServ App prerequisites, then install the LogServ App on your Search Head
    • Review the supported log types reference
    • For Splunk Cloud considerations, see Splunk Cloud Considerations

    Verify Your Data¶

    Run these checks once your first input has read data (step 11 of the Deployment Roadmap, in its 4. Verify Your Data group), before you install the LogServ App. They show whether events arrive, whether the Data TA parsed them, which sourcetypes they got and which cloud they are attributed to.

    Use the index name, not the macro

    The searches below name the index, index=sap_logserv_logs. The sap_logserv_idx_macro macro is defined only where the Data TA or the LogServ App is installed. A distributed or Splunk Cloud search head usually has neither at this point, so a search that uses the macro fails there. If you renamed the data index, put your index name in place of sap_logserv_logs.

    Where to Run the Searches¶

    Run them in Search & Reporting on a search head that searches your indexers: the Splunk Cloud search head, your on-premises search head, or the single instance. All of them only read.

    They look at the last 24 hours of event time. Events from SAP’s queue backlog keep the time they were logged, so while an input is still working through a backlog, widen earliest= (for example to -14d).


    1. Events Arrive and the Data TA Parsed Them¶

    | tstats fillnull_value="(none)" count where index=sap_logserv_logs earliest=-24h by splunk_solution

    The Data TA stamps splunk_solution=splunk_for_sap_logserv on every event it parses. Expect a single row with that value.

    • No rows: nothing has arrived in that time. Check the input on its forwarder (check 5).
    • A (none) row: the Data TA’s rules did not run on those events. Two causes:
      • The Data TA was not on the instance that parsed them. The events keep the base sourcetype sap_logserv_logs, carry no folder fields and keep the whole delivery line as their event text, and they stay that way. Run the Version Check on each heavy forwarder, and distribute the Data TA to any forwarder that lacks it, before more data arrives.
      • On AWS, the SQS-Based S3 input was created with a Source Type other than sap_logserv_logs. The Data TA’s rules run only on that sourcetype, so the events keep the input’s sourcetype, which check 2 shows. Correct the input’s Source Type (step 7 of the Connect guide, step 8 of the Filter and Copy guides); events already indexed stay as they are. The Azure and GCP inputs always send sap_logserv_logs.


    2. Sourcetypes and Cloud¶

    | tstats fillnull_value="(none)" count where index=sap_logserv_logs earliest=-24h by sourcetype, cloud_provider
| sort - count

    fillnull_value must come before count. Without it, tstats leaves out every event that carries no cloud_provider at all.

    • sourcetype: compare the list with Supported Log Types. You see only the types SAP delivers for your landscape. sap_logserv_logs holds what the Data TA does not route; check 4 tells whether that is expected.
    • cloud_provider: each row should name your cloud: aws, azure or gcp. Rows for more than one provider are expected only if you ingest from more than one cloud.
    • (none) in cloud_provider: those events carry no stamp. The Azure and GCP inputs always stamp theirs, so on AWS this means the SQS-Based S3 input has no _meta = cloud_provider::aws line, or read these events before the line went in; see Choose Cloud Attribution. The LogServ App’s dashboards count unstamped events as aws, but your own searches and tstats do not, and the stamp cannot be added to events already indexed.


    3. One Cloud Value per Event¶

    index=sap_logserv_logs earliest=-30d _index_earliest=-15m
| eval cloud_provider_values=mvcount(cloud_provider)
| fillnull value=0 cloud_provider_values
| stats count by cloud_provider_values

    _index_earliest=-15m selects the events indexed in the last 15 minutes, whatever their event time, so the check also works while an input drains a backlog. earliest=-30d only limits how far back the search looks; widen it if your backlog is older.

    Expect 1, and 0 only for AWS events without a stamp. A 2 means the events carry two stamps: the Data TA’s Cloud Provider dropdown is set while the input stamps its own value. See Troubleshooting.

    This check is proven only for two different values (in the lab, an Azure input with the dropdown on AWS gave 2). Whether the same value written twice also shows as 2 (the dropdown on Microsoft Azure for an Azure input, or on AWS for an AWS S3 Direct backfill) has not been tested. A 1 here therefore does not rule it out. Also check that the dropdown is at Not set wherever the Azure or GCP add-on runs or AWS S3 Direct is used (What Gets Stamped).


    4. Routing, by Folder¶

    | tstats fillnull_value="(none)" count where index=sap_logserv_logs sourcetype=sap_logserv_logs earliest=-24h by clz_dir, clz_subdir
| sort - count

    These events stayed under the base sourcetype. Judge them by their folders, not by how many there are: on Azure, the Unix command output that SAP delivers without folder fields can outnumber all other data, and it stays here by design unless you dropped it (Decide Filtering).

    Expected here:

    • (none) / (none): events without folder fields, such as the Azure data under undefined/undefined (Data Delivered Without Folder Fields), and any events that check 1 found without the Data TA.
    • The Secondary log types, which have no routing of their own (Secondary Supported Log Types).
    • Files in folders that the Data TA routes by file path (linux/*, dns/binddns, proxy/squid, windows/*, webdispatcher/accesslog) that are not among the routed files. Add source to the by clause and compare the file paths with Supported Log Types.

    Not expected: the folders the Data TA routes by folder alone. A row for any of them means those events were not routed by the Data TA that parsed them; check that each heavy forwarder runs the current build and has no local/ override of the routes (Version Check):

    hana/hanaaudit, hana/tracelogs, abap/audit, abap/dispatcher, abap/enqueueserver, abap/event, abap/gateway, abap/icm, abap/messageserver, abap/sapstartsrv, abap/workprocess, scc/audit, scc/tracelogs, sap/sapstartsrv, sap/saphostexec, sap/saprouter.


    5. Per-Forwarder Checks¶

    • The Data TA on each heavy forwarder. Run the Version Check on each one: the routing rules run there, not on the Deployment Server.

    • Heavy forwarders that send to Splunk Cloud. From the Splunk Cloud search head, this search must return events for each forwarder; if it returns none, that forwarder is not sending to Splunk Cloud:

      | tstats count where index=_internal host=<HF> earliest=-15m

    • The input’s own log. Forwarders send their _internal data by default, so you can read it from the search head:

      • Azure: index=_internal source=*splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure_queue.log* "done:" shows a line Input '<name>' done: messages=N blobs=N events=N ... per firing (Azure Setup Guide → Validation).
      • GCP: index=_internal source=*splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub.log* "done:" shows a line Input '<name>' done: messages=N objects=N events=N ... per firing (GCP Setup Guide → Validation).
      • AWS: index=_internal source=*aws* level IN (ERROR, WARNING) earliest=-1h lists the errors and warnings of the Splunk Add-on for AWS.


    Next Steps¶

    • If a check fails, find the symptom on Troubleshooting.
    • On AWS, load history with AWS S3 Direct if you need older days.
    • Install the LogServ App and its prerequisites on the search head, then run its Diagnostics page (Data Doctor).

    5. Install the LogServ App

    LogServ App Prerequisites¶

    Use this page before you install the LogServ App (splunk_app_sap_logserv, shown in Splunk Web as Splunk App for SAP LogServ): it lists what the search tier needs beside the App, and who can use and administer it. The ingest tier’s requirements are on Plan and Prerequisites, and the two indexes are created first, on the indexer tier (see Create the indexes).

    Search-Tier Requirements¶

    Install these on the search tier: the search head, the Splunk Cloud search head, or every member of a search head cluster.

    Requirement Version Why
    Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud Platform Splunk Enterprise 9.4.3 or later. Splunk Cloud Platform: Victoria Experience, checked on 10.x (most recently 10.5.2605.10); see Plan and Prerequisites 9.4.3 is the minimum supported version: the platform this release is tested on. The App bundles its own React, @splunk/react-ui, @splunk/visualizations and @xyflow/react, so the floor is a support baseline, not a component dependency.
    Splunk Common Information Model (Splunk_SA_CIM, Splunkbase 1621) 5.0.0 or later The only dependency the App’s app.manifest declares. The App’s CIM event tags (Authentication, Change, Network Sessions, Network Resolution, Web) and its Enterprise Security content build on it. Free on Splunkbase, and bundled with Enterprise Security.
    Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) — (no minimum checked) Required for the Windows panels. No LogServ package extracts fields from XmlWinEventLog, so without it the Windows dashboard’s Event Code, Severity and Service panels stay empty.
    Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) — (no minimum checked) The CIM and Enterprise Security fields of linux_secure. The App parses its other Linux sourcetypes itself.
    KV Store enabled and healthy The dashboards read hourly rollups that scheduled searches write to KV Store; Environment Topology and the App’s settings are stored there too. On a search head cluster, KV Store replication must be healthy.
    Search head cluster optional Supported. Install the App and the add-ons through the deployer; see Dashboard Data: Backfill and Freshness for how the scheduled searches behave on a cluster.

    These add-ons go on the search tier only, not on the Deployment Server, the heavy forwarders or the indexers: the Data TA parses LogServ events before it gives them these sourcetypes, so the add-ons’ parse-time settings never apply to them.

    No standalone Squid Proxy or ISC BIND add-ons

    The parsing of the archived Splunk Add-on for Squid Proxy and Splunk Add-on for ISC BIND is built into the LogServ App. Do not install the standalone add-ons. If either is enabled beside the App, both parse the same events, and the App’s home view shows a dismissible banner recommending that you remove it (Settings > Manage Apps).

    Roles and Access¶

    • Searching the data. Every role that uses the dashboards must be able to search sap_logserv_logs. On Splunk Enterprise the default user role allows *, which matches every index whose name does not start with _, so it and the roles that import it (such as power) can already search the index. Add the index to any role with a narrowed list (Settings > Roles > role > Indexes). On Splunk Cloud, check each role’s Indexes tab the same way.
    • App admins. The App treats only roles named exactly admin, sc_admin or sc_subadmin as admins, and only these roles may write the App’s settings and the dashboards’ KV Store rollups. So only they can open Settings (its AI Assistant and Dashboard Data tabs) and run Clear and Backfill on the dashboard data. A user whose admin role has any other name sees “403 — Admin access required” there. Give the people who run the App one of these three roles; whether a role that imports one of them is enough has not been tested.
    • The audit index. Grant read access to logserv_ai_assistant_audit only as Restricting who can read the audit index describes.

    Enterprise Security content ships enabled

    The App ships its Enterprise Security searches (the splunk_sap_logserv_es_* saved searches, 22 in this release) scheduled and enabled. On a search head without Enterprise Security, we recommend turning them off; see Disabling or tuning the ES content. If you use the AI Assistant’s Security prompts, do not disable the 13 searches they run (a disabled search makes its prompt fail): turn off only their schedule, and disable the other 9 (see the linked section).

    Optional: the AI Assistant

    The AI Assistant ships disabled, and nothing in this page’s table needs it. To use it:

    • Install the Splunk MCP Server (Splunkbase 7931) 1.1.0 or later on the same search head as the App; 1.2.1 or later is recommended (Splunk advisory SVD-2026-1004). The predefined prompts use its Run Saved Search tool, which first shipped in 1.1.0. The App’s health check blocks only versions below 1.0.3 (the CVE-2026-20205 fix) and sets no upper bound; the newest version verified is 2.0.0.
    • Optionally, install the Splunk AI Assistant (Splunkbase 7245) beside it. The LogServ App does not need it: it uses only the MCP Server’s own splunk_run_saved_search and splunk_run_query tools.
    • An admin turns the AI Assistant on and answers its acknowledgements: the liability terms, asked each time it is turned on, and, while audit forwarding is off (the default), the audit-log integrity terms, asked the first time and again when they change (Set Up the AI Assistant).
    • The predefined prompts need no LLM provider or credential. Free-form questions need a provider and its credential, which an admin configures; the shipped default provider is a mock that contacts no vendor.

    The steps are on Set Up the AI Assistant. To turn off or restrict the free-form LLM path, see Restricting the LLM Path.

    Next Steps¶

    • Install the App and Seed the Dashboards

    Install the App and Seed the Dashboards¶

    Use this page to install the LogServ App (splunk_app_sap_logserv, shown in Splunk Web as Splunk App for SAP LogServ) on your search tier, check that it sees your data, and fill the dashboards with the history your index already holds. It covers the last steps of the Deployment Roadmap.

    Before you start

    • Events are arriving in your SAP data index and are routed to their sourcetypes: you have completed Verify Your Data.
    • The search tier meets the LogServ App Prerequisites. KV Store must be enabled; it is by default.
    • You can sign in as a user that holds a role named exactly admin, sc_admin or sc_subadmin. Only these roles see the App’s Settings page, where step 8 runs.

    Upgrading an existing install? Follow Upgrading to This Release instead. It lists the Dashboard Data rows each upgrade must rebuild.

    About the LogServ App¶

    The LogServ App provides:

    • The dashboards and the Environment Topology view: one Environment Health landing page and four groups (Applications, Integration, Security, Platform). See the Dashboards Overview.
    • The Data Doctor (Platform → Diagnostics), which explains empty panels and checks the health of the whole install. See Data Doctor (Diagnostics).
    • Search-time field extractions (EXTRACT / EVAL / FIELDALIAS) for every SAP-specific sourcetype the Data TA routes, and the sap_logserv_idx_macro macro that points the dashboards at your SAP data index.
    • Enterprise Security content: correlation searches, asset and identity feeds and anomaly searches. See Enterprise Security Integration.
    • An AI Assistant panel, which ships disabled. It is optional; see step 9.

    The LogServ App contains no Python code, no REST handlers and no data inputs. The published package is the full-LLM build; to keep the AI Assistant to predefined prompts only, see Restricting the LLM Path.

    Steps¶

    1. Choose where to install
    2. Install the search-tier add-ons
    3. Download the LogServ App
    4. Install the LogServ App
    5. Update the index macro (only if your index is not sap_logserv_logs)
    6. Open the App and check that it sees your data
    7. Run the first health check
    8. Seed the dashboards: the Dashboard Data backfill
    9. Optional: set up the AI Assistant


    1. Where to install¶

    Install the LogServ App on the search tier only:

    • Single Splunk instance: on that instance, next to the Data TA. Splunk merges the two apps’ configurations at runtime.
    • Splunk Enterprise with a separate search tier: on the search head, or on every member of a search head cluster through its deployer (step 4).
    • Splunk Cloud Platform: on the Splunk Cloud search head.

    Never install the LogServ App on heavy forwarders, indexers or the Deployment Server. For where every package goes, see Where Each Package Goes.

    2. Install the search-tier add-ons¶

    Install these Splunkbase add-ons on the same search tier as the App (each search head, the cluster members through the deployer, or the Splunk Cloud search head):

    Add-on Why the App needs it
    Splunk Common Information Model (Splunk_SA_CIM, Splunkbase 1621), version 5.0.0 or later The App declares it as its dependency. The App’s CIM tags and its Enterprise Security content use the CIM data models.
    Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) It extracts the Windows event fields, such as the event code and severity. No LogServ package extracts them, so without it the Windows panels stay empty.
    Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) It provides the CIM and Enterprise Security fields of linux_secure, which the App does not extract. The App parses its other Linux sourcetypes itself, and its dashboards read linux_secure from the raw event text, so they work without it.

    The Squid Proxy and ISC BIND add-ons are not needed: the App includes their parsing. The Splunk MCP Server is needed only for the AI Assistant (step 9). Details: LogServ App Prerequisites.

    3. Download the LogServ App¶

    Download splunk_app_sap_logserv-0.1.2.tar.gz from the GitHub repository.

    4. Install the LogServ App¶

    Use the procedure for your platform.

    Splunk Cloud Platform¶

    Install the LogServ App as a private app on your Splunk Cloud search head. You do not use a deployer on Splunk Cloud Platform.

    Note

    The app installation workflow available to you in Splunk Web depends on your Splunk Cloud Platform Experience: Victoria or Classic. To find your Splunk Cloud Platform Experience, in Splunk Web, click Support & Services > About.

    • Installation instructions for Classic Experience
    • Installation instructions for Victoria Experience

    For the roles and capabilities a Splunk Cloud admin needs, see Splunk Cloud Considerations.

    Splunk Enterprise: single instance or standalone search head¶

    1. From the Splunk Web home screen, click the gear icon next to Apps.
    2. Click Install app from file.
    3. Select the downloaded splunk_app_sap_logserv-0.1.2.tar.gz file and click Upload.
    4. If Splunk Enterprise prompts you to restart, do so.
    5. Check that the app appears in the list of apps. On the server it is at $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/splunk_app_sap_logserv.

    Splunk Enterprise: search head cluster¶

    Distribute the App, and the add-ons of step 2, with the cluster’s deployer. Do not install them on the members one by one.

    1. On the deployer, extract the tarball into $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/shcluster/apps/, so that the App is at $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/shcluster/apps/splunk_app_sap_logserv.

    2. On the deployer, push the bundle to the cluster:

      $SPLUNK_HOME/bin/splunk apply shcluster-bundle -target https://<any-member>:8089

    3. Wait for the members to finish the restart the push starts, if it needs one.

    The cluster’s captain runs each scheduled search on one member, and KV Store replicates the App’s collections to every member, so you run the backfill of step 8 once, from any member. See Behavior with multiple search heads.

    5. Update the index macro¶

    Skip this step if your SAP data index is sap_logserv_logs.

    The dashboards find your data through the search macro sap_logserv_idx_macro. Both the LogServ App and the Data TA ship this macro. On a search head that has both apps, such as a single instance or a Splunk Cloud stack with the Data TA, change it in both apps: the scheduled rollups and the Dashboard Data backfill use the App’s copy, while the live dashboard panels can use the Data TA’s copy. On a search head without the Data TA, change the App’s copy.

    Follow the single procedure in Renaming an Index, then check the result in step 6.

    6. Open the App and check that it sees your data¶

    1. In Splunk Web, open Splunk App for SAP LogServ. It opens on Environment Health, with a navigation rail on the left: Environment Health, Topology, Applications, Integration, Security, Platform, and below a divider Settings (admin roles only) and About. The Dashboards Overview describes the rail, the header and the controls every dashboard shares.

    2. In the Search app, run:

      `sap_logserv_idx_macro` | stats count by sourcetype

      It must return events from your SAP data index, split across the SAP sourcetypes.

    If the search returns nothing:

    • Check that events are arriving: Verify Your Data. The Data TA parses and routes the events where the inputs run (your heavy forwarders, a single instance, or a Splunk Cloud stack that runs the inputs itself); your cloud’s ingest add-on collects them.
    • Check that the macro points at your index (step 5).
    • Check that your role can search the index. On Splunk Enterprise the stock user role allows *, which matches every index whose name does not start with _, so a user who holds that role, or a role that imports it, can already search your SAP data index. A role with a narrowed list of allowed indexes (Settings → Roles → role → Indexes) needs your SAP data index added.

    7. Run the first health check¶

    Open Platform → Diagnostics and let its checks finish. Confirm that the summary names your SAP data index and the add-ons of step 2, then click Download report (PDF) and keep the report as the install’s starting point. On a fresh install the History column reads NEVER BUILT, or INCOMPLETE once the first hourly run has written an hour or two; that is expected until step 8.

    Details: First health check after install.

    8. Seed the dashboards: the Dashboard Data backfill¶

    Most dashboard panels read hourly rollups that start empty. Without a backfill they fill in one hour at a time from the next hourly run, so any install whose index already holds events needs this step: events loaded with AWS S3 Direct, ingest that ran before the App was installed, or a few days of normal arrival.

    1. Sign in as a user with a role named admin, sc_admin or sc_subadmin.
    2. Open Settings → Dashboard Data.
    3. In Backfill window, pick a window that covers the history your index holds: 30 days is the default; 60, 90, 180 and 365 days and a Custom range of whole UTC days, back to the 365-day retention, are also offered. After an AWS S3 Direct load, use a custom range that matches the dates you loaded.
    4. Click Run backfill. Start it outside the nightly retention window (00:34-00:58, 01:30-01:58 and 02:34-02:36 in the search head’s time zone), and keep the page open until every row has finished.
    5. Go back to Platform → Diagnostics and click Re-run checks. A row reads COMPLETE once its rollup holds data reaching back at least 29 days, so it needs events of that rollup’s log types at least that old in your index. A row whose log types you do not collect stays NEVER BUILT, and a row with less history in the index reads INCOMPLETE; neither means the backfill failed. If the backfill finishes with issues, Settings → Dashboard Data says so and marks the affected rollups in its table: run the backfill again to retry them.

    Details, including the late-arriving data check: Dashboard Data: Backfill and Freshness.

    Enterprise Security content runs by default

    The App’s 22 Enterprise Security searches (splunk_sap_logserv_es_*) ship enabled and run on this search head whether or not Enterprise Security is installed. If this search head has no Enterprise Security, consider turning them off: see Disabling or tuning the ES content. The AI Assistant’s Security prompts run 13 of these searches on demand, so if you use those prompts, turn off only the schedules of those 13, as that section describes.

    9. Optional: set up the AI Assistant¶

    The AI Assistant ships disabled: no button, panel or route appears until an admin turns it on. To use it:

    • Install the Splunk MCP Server (Splunkbase App 7931) 1.1.0 or later on the same search head as the LogServ App; 1.2.1 or later is recommended, because it fixes SVD-2026-1004. The predefined prompts run through the MCP Server’s Run Saved Search tool, which first shipped in 1.1.0. The App’s health check only refuses versions below 1.0.3 (the CVE-2026-20205 fix), so 1.0.3 to 1.0.5 pass that check but the predefined prompts fail. There is no upper version limit. Installation and authentication: Splunk MCP Setup.
    • Grant the MCP Server’s mcp_tool_execute capability to every role that will use the AI Assistant. The MCP Server (version 1.1.0) grants it only to admin and sc_admin. See Roles and Capabilities.
    • As an admin, open Settings → AI Assistant → General, turn on Enable AI Assistant and click Save Defaults. Accept the AI Assistant — Liability terms dialog that opens and, while audit forwarding is off (the default), the Audit log integrity dialog after it; nothing is saved until you do. The liability dialog appears every time the AI Assistant is turned on, and again when its terms change. The AI Assistant button then appears at the right end of the header’s second row.

    If the panel opens a setup wizard instead of the chat, the MCP Server is missing or older than the App accepts, or your role lacks mcp_tool_execute: see Splunk MCP Setup.

    The predefined prompts need no LLM provider credential. The shipped default provider is Mock: until an admin selects a provider and stores its credential, a typed question gets a canned mock reply and no vendor is contacted.

    Full procedure: Set Up the AI Assistant.

    Next Steps¶

    • Explore the dashboards: Dashboards Overview.
    • Keep the dashboards current and rebuild late-arriving days: Dashboard Data: Backfill and Freshness.
    • Change what is filtered at ingest: Configuring Filters.
    • Turn on the AI Assistant: Set Up the AI Assistant.
    • Something does not look right: Troubleshooting.

    Configure and Operate

    Configuring Filters¶

    This page is the reference for the Data TA’s filters: what each field does, how the rules combine, how to check and change them, and the AWS Lambda filter. When you set up the Data TA for the first time, decide first with Decide Filtering, and distribute the Data TA with Distribute the Data TA to Heavy Forwarders.

    Overview¶

    The Splunk TA for SAP LogServ provides two complementary approaches to filtering LogServ data — you can use either one independently or combine them for defense-in-depth filtering. (A third, lighter layer exists on the Azure and GCP ingest add-ons: their inputs accept optional include_filters / exclude_filters substring patterns applied to the object path before download, a cheap pre-filter — the canonical allow/deny policy still lives on this page’s Filters tab.)

    Native TA Index-Time Filtering AWS Lambda-Based Filtering
    Where it runs Inside Splunk at index time In AWS Lambda, before data reaches Splunk
    Configured via Splunk Web UI (Configuration → Filters) Lambda environment variables or migration config
    Works with All deployment scenarios (Connect, Filter, Copy) S3 Filter and Connect-to-Filter migration only
    What it filters Raw NDJSON events via TRANSFORMS queue routing S3 event notifications: the Lambda downloads each object and forwards its notification only if at least one record passes
